title: Claude development pipeline configuration
description: Per-repo pipeline contract, read by both the hooks and the skills so they cannot disagree. Two valid shapes: a FULL onboarding config (version, branches, worktrees, commands - what /pipeline-kit:init writes), or a PROTECTION-ONLY config (version plus protectedPaths and/or unprotectedPaths) that configures protected-files.cjs without enrolling the repo in branch enforcement, claims or session registration. The presence of `branches` is what marks a repo as onboarded.

x-driftChecks.why: Build's change-time gate skips silently without it
the review gate's reviewer picks its own tier, at the top of the list
no tier to propose when two review rounds share one cause

x-driftChecksNote: Keys a current config should carry whose absence DEGRADES a gate rather than invalidating the file. Read by pipeline-session.cjs to say one line at SessionStart, and by /pipeline-kit:init in update mode. It lives here because the schema already answers `what should a config contain`, and a second copy of that answer is the duplication that has shipped the same bug twice in this repo. Add an entry when a new key silently changes behaviour by being absent - not for every optional key, since a notice that fires on noise trains the reader to skim the banner.

version.description: Schema version. Bump only on a breaking shape change.

kind.description: 'local' means the .scratch/ markdown convention; 'none' disables the ticket gate.

repo.description: owner/name. Cached so hooks never shell out to `gh repo view`.

ghAccount.description: Account to pin per command via GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user <this>). The globally active gh account is mutable and a concurrent session can flip it mid-run.

issueTypes.description: Read and write GitHub issue types instead of category labels. true maps the kit's categories to the types Spec, Feature, Bug, Chore, Refactor, Documentation, Spike and Task; a map names a different type for any category, and the rest keep those names. Absent or false: category labels, as before.

priority.description: The organization single-select issue field holding a ticket's priority.

area.description: The organization single-select issue field holding a ticket's area. Plan groups tickets by it where no module label says what a ticket edits.

fields.description: Organization issue fields to read and write instead of priority and area labels. Absent: labels, as before.

owner.description: The organization that owns the project.

statusField.description: The project's single-select status field. Defaults to Status.

newStatus.description: The status an issue gets in the project when it has none, such as Backlog: a newly added issue, or one the project's own auto-add put there. An issue that already has a status keeps it. Absent: no status is set.

project.description: An organization project that Capture and Shape add every issue they file to. The project's own auto-add workflow cannot be set through the API. Absent: nothing is added to a project.

trunk.description: The single long-lived branch. Under GitHub Flow this is also the default branch, which is what makes PR closing keywords work.

protected.description: Branches the guard refuses direct edits on.

root.description: Repo-relative directory for linked worktrees. Paths outside the blessed root prompt on EnterWorktree.

setup.description: Repo-relative script run once per fresh worktree. Must be idempotent.

commands.description: Verification commands. 'build' and 'test' are the gates a lane runs before claiming a ticket done.

format.description: The formatter itself, run by Build and Land when 'formatCheck' fails. Writing the fix by hand is what an agent is worst at and most likely to widen past the ticket.

formatCheck.description: The read-only check, run beside 'build' and 'test' at every verification step.

mode.description: 'inline' edits CHANGELOG.md directly and conflicts when branches run in parallel. 'fragments' writes one file per change under dir/ and assembles at release.

dir.description: Fragment directory. Required when mode is 'fragments'.

update.description: What the Land lane does about the repository wiki after a release, using the changelog section it just dated as the brief. 'approve' pushes without asking - a wiki has no draft state, so that publishes immediately and irreversibly. Omitted behaves as 'ask' where the repo has a wiki, and does nothing where it does not.

protectedPaths.description: Extra files this project's agents must never hand-edit, on top of the shared defaults (.env, lockfiles, node_modules, build output, .git). Use for generated files a generator owns. Keeps language-specific rules out of the shared hook.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regex matched against the absolute path with forward slashes.

why.description: Shown in the denial. Say what owns the file, so the reader knows what to change instead.

trigger.description: 'draft-on-push' creates a draft release when the version changes on trunk; publishing the draft is a separate manual act.

bump.description: Whether Land confirms the version it derives from the changelog. 'ask', also when absent, confirms every time. 'auto' uses the derived version without asking when the changelog categories alone decide it, which needs every heading to be one of Keep a Changelog's six and a current version with no prerelease suffix: before 1.0, PATCH for only Fixed and Security entries and MINOR otherwise, never 1.0.0; from 1.0, only when nothing is under Changed or Removed. A person still sees the version in the release PR, which Land never merges, before any tag exists.

models.description: Model tier per pipeline phase. A closed set, unlike `commands`: a repo can invent a build command, but it cannot invent a phase, and a tier no lane reads is a tier nothing spends. Cost is a tie-breaker only; intelligence wins on anything that ships.

discovery.description: The Explore subagents Capture and Build spawn before changing anything.

build.description: The model Plan names per recommended ticket when it dispatches the session.

review.description: The reviewer Build's review gate spawns each round. A spawn given no tier picks its own and reaches for the top of the list.

reviewEscalation.description: The reviewer Build escalates to when two rounds share one root cause. The lane names the model and asks first, unless policy.agentsMayEscalate is true.

agentsMayClose.description: Whether an agent may close a tracker issue without asking first. False, the default, does not mean never: a lane that finds a ticket finished, not reproducible or superseded posts the finding and puts the close to the user, then acts on the answer. True lets it close an unambiguous outcome unprompted.

agentsMayMerge.description: Whether the Build lane may start merge-await without asking once its PR holds a queue position. False, the default, asks at Build step 10b: merge when the turn comes, hold for review, or take remarks. True skips that question only when all three conditions step 10b lists hold: the queued head passed every build and test command the repo configures, of which there is at least one, the last review round found nothing Critical or Important and nothing but the changelog changed after it, and the review never reached its escalation point. Otherwise the lane asks as before. merge-await then merges only a PR that is first in line, with green checks and a head that has not moved since it joined the queue other than by its own branch update, and it stops for a person on failed checks, conflicts, requested changes or a lost queue place. On a repo with no CI it has no checks to wait for, so nothing tests the merged result.

agentsMayEscalate.description: Whether Build may escalate its reviewer to models.reviewEscalation without asking, when two review rounds share one root cause. False, the default, names the model and asks. True escalates and reports which model reviewed and why; with no models.reviewEscalation the lane still asks. A user's own rule to ask before a given model still applies. An escalated review still makes Build ask before the merge, whatever policy.agentsMayMerge says.

maxParallel.description: How many tickets Plan may recommend starting at once. Defaults to 4 when absent. Worktrees share one object store, refs and config behind single-writer locks, so the ceiling is the repo's git contention rather than the machine's cores - raise it only while watching for index.lock failures.

unprotectedPaths.description: Paths this project declares legitimately writable, SUBTRACTED from the shared defaults (.env, lockfiles, node_modules, build output). Use when a default is simply wrong here - `out/` is generated in most repos and is the deliverable in some. Cannot lift either floor: .git/, and .claude/pipeline.json itself - this list is read out of that file, so a rule it could switch off would not be a rule. Without an escape like this, a wrong default does not prevent the write: it pushes it onto a shell command that no PreToolUse hook can observe.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regex matched against the absolute path with forward slashes.

why.description: Say why this path is legitimate output for this project. Read by humans reviewing the opt-out.

validation.description: Project-specific checks Build must pass. `ticket` asks whether the work is sound; `change` asks whether the approach chosen to do it is. They are different questions, and running the first list twice only ever asks the first one.

ticket.description: Run at Build step 1, against the ticket. A ticket can be coherent about this codebase and still ask for something the domain does not permit.

name.description: Short label for the check, used when reporting which checks ran.

how.description: Instruction for performing it, naming the authority to consult - a skill, a document, or a command.

onFail.description: Where a failing ticket goes: capture to re-investigate, shape to be scoped, stop to report and halt.

change.description: Run at Build step 5, against the chosen approach, and again whenever implementation turns up a dependency step 5 did not name. A ticket can be sound while the rule the fix relies on is not - and that rule is usually discovered while writing the code, after the ticket gate is behind you. Build demands cited authority for such rules in every repo; this list is where a project names the authority it wants cited.

name.description: Short label for the check, used when reporting which checks ran.

how.description: Instruction for performing it, naming the authority that settles it - a source file to read, a command to run, a test to compile. A rule inferred from this codebase's own model is not cited: the code can be wrong, and so can a comment.

onFail.description: What a failing approach does: replan to return to step 5 and derive a new one from the authority, stop to report and halt. Never `capture` or `shape` - the ticket is not what failed.
